blocks.note: Choose future, future perfect, and past conditional from the relevant time viewpoint, including future forms after time conjunctions and conjectural uses; the hygiene gate excludes the one judgment-dependent future alternative.
Keep present or imperfect with da for an activity still in progress at the reference time, and place a completed event before another past event with the appropriate pluperfect.

Contrast imperfect background, state, habit, politeness, and play-frame uses with bounded passato prossimo or passato remoto events. The synthetic passage sets and all printed alternatives are omitted by plan or hygiene gate.
Use stare plus gerund only when the predicate supports an event viewed in progress, leaving state predicates and other incompatible readings in a simple tense.

Replace finite clauses or English -ing forms with a gerund, participle, or infinitive only when subject control, time relation, agreement, and syntactic function license it; the hygiene gate removes the one judgment-dependent alternative.
Select the subjunctive after volition, evaluation, belief, reaction, non-assertion, and occurrence predicates, then apply the tense relationship imposed by the governing clause.
Use the subjunctive after purpose, concession, hypothesis, evaluation, and nonfactual time conjunctions while preserving the semantic relation expressed by the source sentence.

Choose indicative or subjunctive in relative, impersonal, and indirect-question clauses according to specificity, assertion, evaluation, and the governing expression; the hygiene gate excludes one variable indefinite-relative answer.

Translate English modal wording by function rather than word-for-word, choosing future, conditional, dovere, potere, sapere, riuscire, an unmodalized perception verb, or a subjunctive construction as required.
